propositions.text: Applicant seeks to set aside FPSLREB adjudicator's decision excluding LP-04 position from bargaining unit under FPSLRA 59(1)(g)
propositions.quote: The applicant seeks to set aside the decision of an adjudicator of the Federal Public Sector Labour Relations and Employment Board (the FPSLREB) in Treasury Board (Department of Justice) v. Association of Justice Counsel, 2020 FPSLREB 59.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant seeks to set aside the FPSLREB adjudicator's decision excluding the LP-04 position from the bargaining unit under FPSLRA 59(1)(g).

propositions.text: Adjudicator found LP-04 incumbent advised on Privacy Act and Access to Information Act in labour relations-sensitive matters
propositions.quote: the adjudicator determined that the incumbent of the position in question was sometimes called upon to provide advice on issues under the Privacy Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. P-21 and the Access to Information Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. A-1 in the context of labour relations-sensitive matters.

propositions.text: Adjudicator concluded sufficient intersection of labour relations, staffing and classification matters justified exclusion under 59(1)(g) for conflict of interest
propositions.quote: there was accordingly a “sufficient intersection of labour relations, staffing and classification matters” to justify the exclusion due to the potential for a conflict of interest under paragraph 59(1)(g) of the FPSLRA.

propositions.text: Adjudicator found exclusion under 59(1)(c) not warranted as occupant did not advise on labour relations, staffing or classification issues themselves
propositions.quote: The adjudicator, however, determined that an exclusion under paragraph 59(1)(c) of the FPSLRA was not warranted as the occupant of the position did not provide advice on labour relations, staffing or classification issues, themselves.

paragraphs.summary: The adjudicator found the LP-04 incumbent advised on privacy and access issues in labour relations-sensitive matters, justifying exclusion under 59(1)(g) but not 59(1)(c).

propositions.text: Relevant FPSLRA provisions 59(1)(c), (g), and (h) define managerial or confidential position exclusions
propositions.quote: The relevant provisions in the FPSLRA provide: Application Demande 59 (1) ... (c) the occupant of the position provides advice on labour relations, staffing or classification; ... (g) the occupant of the position has duties and responsibilities ... for reasons of conflict of interest ...; or (h) the occupant of the position has ... duties and responsibilities confidential to the occupant of a position described in paragraph (b), (c), (d) or (f).

paragraphs.summary: The court sets out relevant FPSLRA provisions 59(1)(c), (g), and (h) defining managerial or confidential position exclusions.

propositions.text: Applicant asserts adjudicator's decision was unreasonable for two principal reasons
propositions.quote: Before us, the applicant asserts that the decision of the adjudicator was unreasonable, principally for two reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant asserts the adjudicator's decision was unreasonable for two main reasons.

propositions.text: Applicant argues adjudicator unreasonably interpreted FPSLRA provisions narrowly limiting labour relations exclusions to 59(1)(c) or (h)
propositions.quote: The applicant says that the adjudicator unreasonably interpreted the relevant statutory provisions, which should be read narrowly as they limit the constitutionally-protected right to join and be represented by a trade union.

propositions.text: Applicant submits Parliament intended all labour relations exclusions under 59(1)(c) or (h), not 59(1)(g)
propositions.quote: The applicant submits that the text, context and purpose of the relevant provisions indicate that Parliament contemplated that all labour relations-related exclusions would fall under either paragraph 59(1)(c) or (h) of the FPSLRA

propositions.text: Applicant contends interpreting 59(1)(g) to include labour relations duties broadens exclusions impermissibly
propositions.quote: it was therefore not reasonable to interpret paragraph 59(1)(g) of the Act as including duties in relations to labour relations matters that do not rise to the level of being covered by either paragraph 59(1)(c) or (h) of the FPSLRA.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant argues the adjudicator unreasonably interpreted FPSLRA, wrongly broadening labour relations exclusions under 59(1)(g) beyond 59(1)(c) or (h).

propositions.text: Applicant asserts adjudicator unreasonably relied on incumbent's seniority and experience, irrelevant to duties inquiry
propositions.quote: the applicant asserts that the adjudicator unreasonably premised his decision in large part on the fact that the incumbent in the LP-04 position within the CILP was a senior, experienced lawyer.

propositions.text: Applicant says case law requires examining duties, not incumbent's attributes
propositions.quote: case law of the FPSLREB requires examination of the duties required of the position as opposed to the attributes of the incumbent.

propositions.text: Applicant argues if seniority mattered, no senior government lawyer could unionize, contrary to Parliament's intent
propositions.quote: were it otherwise, no senior government lawyer could ever be unionized, which was clearly not the intent of Parliament when it extended collective bargaining rights to lawyers working for the federal government in 2005.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant argues the adjudicator unreasonably relied on the incumbent's seniority, contrary to case law and Parliament's intent.

propositions.text: Court disagrees with both applicant submissions
propositions.quote: With respect, I disagree with both submissions.

paragraphs.summary: The court disagrees with both of the applicant's submissions.

propositions.text: Applicant cites no authority that 59(1)(g) cannot apply to conflicts from advice like incumbent's
propositions.quote: the applicant has cited no authority in support of his contention that paragraph 59(1)(g) of the FPSLRA cannot apply to conflicts or potential conflicts arising from the provision of advice of precisely the sort given by the incumbent in the LP-04 position in this case.

propositions.text: This case is similar to earlier FPSLREB decisions excluding incumbents providing advice with potential impacts like here
propositions.quote: this case is similar to earlier decisions of the FPSLREB ... where incumbents were excluded because they provided advice on topics that had potential impacts akin to those in the present case

propositions.text: Prior FPSLREB decisions excluded incumbents providing advice with potential labour relations impacts
propositions.quote: see, for example, Canada (Auditor General) v. Public Service Alliance of Canada, [1980] C.P.S.S.R.B. No. 2 ... Treasury Board v. PSAC, 2016 PSLREB 84

paragraphs.summary: The applicant cites no authority against 59(1)(g) applying here; prior FPSLREB decisions excluded similar advice-giving incumbents.

propositions.text: Paragraph 59(1)(g) of FPSLRA is broad, granting FPSLREB wide discretion to exclude employees for duties and responsibilities
propositions.quote: the provision “[…] confers on the PSLRB a very broad discretion to exclude an employee on the basis of aspects of his or her duties and responsibilities […].”

propositions.text: Treasury Board (Correctional Service of Canada) v. Public Service Alliance of Canada confirms broad discretion under 59(1)(g)
propositions.quote: As noted in Treasury Board (Correctional Service of Canada) v. Public Service Alliance of Canada, 2012 PSLRB 46 ... at para. 70, the provision “[…] confers on the PSLRB a very broad discretion to exclude an employee on the basis of aspects of his or her duties and responsibilities […].”

paragraphs.summary: Paragraph 59(1)(g) is broad, granting FPSLREB wide discretion to exclude employees based on duties, per prior case law.

propositions.text: Adjudicator's interpretation of paragraph 59(1)(g) was reasonable
propositions.quote: The adjudicator’s interpretation of paragraph 59(1)(g) of the FPSLRA was therefore reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the adjudicator's interpretation of paragraph 59(1)(g) reasonable.

propositions.text: Court disagrees adjudicator based decision largely on incumbent's seniority
propositions.quote: I disagree that he premised the decision in large part on the fact that the incumbent in the LP-04 position was a senior, experienced lawyer.

propositions.text: Adjudicator's comments about seniority respond to employer's suggestion about delegating labour relations-sensitive discussions to junior lawyer
propositions.quote: The comments made by the adjudicator ... must be read in context and are responsive to suggestions that the employer could have ensured all labour relations-sensitive discussions were held with the more junior excluded lawyer in the CILP.

propositions.text: Adjudicator explained why excluding senior position was permissible
propositions.quote: In the impugned paragraphs, the adjudicator merely explained why it was permissible for the employer to also exclude a senior position within the CILP.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the adjudicator did not base decision largely on seniority but explained why excluding senior position was permissible.

propositions.text: Adjudicator highlighted duties causing conflict, such as advising on privacy and access issues in litigation with bargaining agents
propositions.quote: the adjudicator highlights the duties assigned to the LP-04 position that gave rise to a conflict of interest, such as providing advice in respect of privacy or access to information issues in connection with litigation between the employer and the bargaining agents.

propositions.text: Respondent noted evidence that incumbent performed such duties before and after CILP reorganization, even without managing subordinates
propositions.quote: there was evidence before the adjudicator that indicated that such duties had been performed by the incumbent both before and after the reorganization in the CILP, when the incumbent was no longer charged with managing subordinates

paragraphs.summary: The adjudicator focused on duties causing conflict, supported by evidence incumbent performed them before and after reorganization.

propositions.text: Adjudicator did not unreasonably base decision on incumbent's experience
propositions.quote: The adjudicator therefore did not unreasonably base his decision on the fact that the incumbent in the LP-04 position within the CILP possessed significant experience.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the adjudicator did not unreasonably rely on the incumbent's experience.

propositions.text: Application dismissed with costs fixed at $2,500
propositions.quote: I would accordingly dismiss this application, with costs, fixed in the agreed-upon all-inclusive amount of $2,500.00, which I believe to be reasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the application with costs fixed at $2,500.
